title: docs(skills): teach one naming rule, every package-authored metadata name starts with its namespace
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9DWyW8k3qL1ZSS5TK1cXcDAs)_

Fixes #30805

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:发布的 authoring skills 现在只教一条命名规则——包里写的每个元数据名都以包的 namespace 开头(`crm_send_email`、`crm_sales_rep`),例外只有字段、对象扩展、容器视图和翻译;全部示例和 evals 里的裸名已改成带前缀。
- 为什么改:落实 #30798 裁决 C 的第二阶段,让 AI 在第三阶段把裸名变成拒收之前就已经按一种写法写名字。
- 风险与回滚:只改 `skills/**` 文档和 evals,不动任何代码、schema 或行为;回滚就是还原这一个 PR。
- 先看:`skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md` 第 123 行新加的规则段,以及下方的改名表和保留名单。
- 两分钟验证:`node scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs` 全绿(每个文件都在原天花板内,靠同文件删减付费);`pnpm --dir ui run check:skill-eval-tokens` 通过。
- 需要你做的:按 Tier H 走受治理审批;下方 Open questions 里有三处需要席位或你拍板的保留项(裸对象名、连接器 id、能力名)。

## What changes

`objectstack-platform/SKILL.md` states the rule once, as a new paragraph right after the object rule:
every metadata name a package authors starts with its namespace (flows, actions, hooks, apps, pages,
dashboards, reports, datasets, queues, positions, permission sets, skills). The exceptions are fields,
object extensions and container views (derived from a prefixed object), and translations (the namespace,
an underscore, then the locale). The paragraph is taught as the authoring contract. It also says what
origin/main enforces today, read off the code:

- `defineStack` refuses a bare object name (`validateObjectNamespacePrefix`, `packages/spec/src/kernel/namespace-prefix.ts`).
- `os build` refuses a bare doc name (`docs/namespace-prefix`, an error).
- `os lint`'s `naming/namespace-prefix` warns only when one package declares an app, page, dashboard,
  flow, action, report or dataset name twice (`packages/cli/src/commands/lint.ts` around L280-330).

The old sentence in that paragraph said `os lint` warns on every bare UI or automation name whenever a
namespace is set. That is false on main, so it is removed. #30804 (open) widens that lint. If it lands
first, this paragraph's last sentence must be re-matched to its type list before merge. If this PR lands
first, #30804's PR owes that one-sentence update.

Every example and eval in `skills/**` that showed or generated a bare non-object name now carries the
prefix. Snippets with no manifest use `crm`. Snippets with their own package context keep it: `todo` for
the i18n app-todo mirror, which already uses `todo_app`. Cross-references move together: action targets,
`dashboardName` / `reportName`, approver and queue values, `permissionSets`, `skills`, `action_` tool
names, translation keys and eval `must_contain` tokens.

`skills/README.md` "Conventions enforced across skills" now teaches the same rule. It keeps the existing
short-object-name convention for snippets, with no object-level `namespace` and no `tableName`.

| skills/README.md | "Short object names; no `namespace`, no `tableName`." | the one rule plus its exemptions, then "Short object names in snippets; no object-level `namespace`, no `tableName`." |

Not renamed, because they are exempt as nested names: validation rule names, flow node ids, edge targets,
widget ids, dataset dimensions and measures, assignment-rule entries, nav item ids, params, and container
view keys.

### Held, not renamed (report per the dispatch's external-caller stop)

- **Connector ids** `stripe`, `github_mcp`, `warehouse_api`, `legacy_erp` (integration-recipes.md),
  `erp_api` (datasources.md), `sap_erp` (upgrade eval 3) and the platform `slack` connector. The id is
  what credentials and inbound calls name.
- **The api flow `carrier_callback`.** Its name is a segment of the inbound URL the carrier calls
  (`…/hooks/carrier_callback/carrier`).
- **The datasource `warehouse`.** Its name keys the `OS_DATASOURCE_WAREHOUSE_PASSWORD` variable.
- **Capability names** `view_pii` and `expense.approve_request`. Their grammar is dotted, and how a prefix
  applies to it is a phase-3 question.
- **Function handler names** (`normalize`, `helpdesk.aiTriageStub`, `billing.sync`). They are not a
  metadata type. **Knowledge source id** `support_kb`. It is not stack metadata.
- **Bare object names in snippets** (`account`, `lead`, `task`, …). These are outside this card, which
  covers non-object names. See Open questions.

Package-wide (all authored and eval files under `skills/**` this PR touches, ceil of bytes over 4):
7633 → 7635 lines, 97336 → 97353 tokens (+17). The +17 is the eval fixtures, which are measured but not
ratcheted, plus `skills/README.md`, which is outside the ratchet. Every ratcheted file is at or under its
ceiling.

## Why

Decision #30798 ruled C (maintainer, verbatim: 「同意 c」). Every package-authored metadata name carries its
namespace, in three phases. This is phase 2, the AI-authoring half: the published skills teach the one rule
before phase 3 makes a bare name a refusal.

## Tests

No code changes, so there are no new unit tests. The gates that read `skills/**` are what judge this diff.
Families derived by `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`
(48), run locally at head `7fd40067`, each exit code recorded as `COMMAND :: exit CODE`:

- 47 of 48 exit 0. They include `node scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs` (and `--self-test`),
  `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec run check:skill-examples` (after the
  `@objectstack/client-react...` closure build), `check:skill-docs`, `check:skill-refs`,
  `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint run check:doc-formula-expressions` (after the `@objectstack/lint...`
  closure build), `pnpm check:skill-top-level-keys`, `check:skill-identifier-liveness`,
  `check:skill-frame-sync`, `check:skill-compatibility`, `check:nul-bytes`, `check:doc-authoring`,
  `check:pm-governed-merges` and `pnpm --dir ui exec vitest run scripts/`.
- `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exited 3 with "PREREQUISITE NOT MET — this gate reads built output,
  and some package has no dist/". Nothing was measured. The gate reads `packages/**/dist`, which this diff
  does not touch. The PR's CI check-run is the reading for it.
- `--ran` reconciliation: "48 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 47 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED (1 DERIVED from
  a recorded exit 3)", with 0 unrun.
- Run outside the derived list: `pnpm --dir ui run check:skill-eval-tokens --self-test` and
  `pnpm --dir ui run check:skill-eval-tokens` exited 0 ("Every must_contain token is taught by its own
  skill bundle"). `pnpm lint` exited 0.

## Acceptance notes

- **Out of scope, reported to the seat and not fixed here:** `skills/objectui/guides/project-setup.md`
  L199-221 imports `defineConfig` from `@objectstack/runtime`, which exports no `defineConfig` on main.
  The snippet also nests `objects` under `apps[]` with the name `my-app`. It carries no `os:check`
  marker, so no gate compiles it.
- Under the rule, an app named exactly `crm` is bare, because `validateObjectNamespacePrefix` checks
  for the namespace followed by an underscore. That is why the action URL now points at
  `crm_enterprise`.

## Open questions

1. **Bare object names in skill snippets.** Most snippets use short object names (`account`, `lead`) by
   the README convention, while ADR-0129 requires the prefix once a namespace is set. Recommendation: a
   separate card after phase 3, so this PR stays at the card's non-object scope.
2. **Connector, inbound api flow and datasource names** (held above). Recommendation: keep them, and have
   phase 3 exempt names an external caller or a variable spells, or rename them with a migration note.
3. **Dotted capability names.** Phase 3 should state how the prefix applies (`crm.view_pii` or
   `crm_view_pii`).

## Verification

1. Check out the branch and run `node scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs`. Every ratcheted file
   reads at or under its ceiling, and no ceiling moved.
2. Run `pnpm --dir ui run check:skill-eval-tokens`. It passes, including the renamed
   `action_crm_escalate_case` token.
3. Read `skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md` L123 against `packages/spec/src/kernel/namespace-prefix.ts`
   and `packages/cli/src/commands/lint.ts`. The enforcement sentence matches main.
4. Run `git grep -nE "name: '(lead_conversion|support_intake|sales_rep|escalate_case|case_management)'" -- skills`.
   It returns nothing.

## Human Minimum

- [x] 1. Schemas start as Zod; `packages/spec` holds no runtime logic. (`packages/spec` untouched.)
- [x] 2. Every name I added uses the casing for its kind.
- [x] 3. No formatter ran; `pnpm lint` passes.
- [x] 4. One issue, one branch off an up-to-date `main`, one pull request.
- [x] 5. A change that publishes carries a changeset, and both declaration lines are filled in here and in the changeset.
- [x] 6. `packages/spec` touched: its generated artifacts are regenerated and committed. (Not touched.)
- [x] 7. No hand edits to `content/docs/references/`, `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md` or `content/docs/releases/`.
- [x] 8. Title, body and comments are in English, apart from the fleet's required `## 维护者速读` summary.
